subject: Mental Models
title: The Dunning-Kruger Effect
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Dunning-Kruger Effect.

hook.text: A bank robber covered his face with lemon juice, believing it made him invisible to cameras. He was wrong.

buildup.text: Psychologists Dunning and Kruger studied him. They found beginners wildly overestimate their own skill level.

discovery.text: The less you know, the less you realize how much you don't know. Ignorance feels like confidence.

twist.text: Experts show the opposite pattern. They underestimate themselves because they see how much remains to learn.

climax.text: The cure is deliberate practice and honest feedback. Skill and self-awareness grow together over time.

punchline.text: Confidence without skill is a warning sign.

quiz.question: What happens to self-assessment as expertise increases?
options: Experts become more aware of what they don't know and become humble
Expertise has no effect on self-assessment
